newsitem.title: UK: CRICKET-ENGLAND DENY ADVANTAGE WITH PITCH SWITCH.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-ENGLAND DENY ADVANTAGE WITH PITCH SWITCH.

text.p: England officials denied on Thursday that chairman of selectors David Graveney was responsible for switching the pitch for the fourth test against Australia.
The strip was changed to an adjoining one, prompting speculation that England were seeking to gain an advantage by negating the strengths of Australian leg-spinner Shane Warne.

Tour manager Alan Crompton wrote a letter of complaint to the England and Wales Cricket Board (ECB), saying it was "totally inappropriate for the chairman of selectors to have anything to do with the choice of pitch".
But chief executive Tim Lamb told a news conference: "I can assure you that David Graveney did not make that decision. It was taken by Yorkshire in conjunction with our pitch consultant Harry Brind.

"A conversation took place between David Graveney and Harry Brind and it is that which came to Alan Crompton's notice. It is entirely good practice for the chairman of selectors to know what sort of pitch is being prepared for a test.
"I can understand why people thought David was involved, but he is a bit concerned about a perception of sharp practice."
Lamb said the pitch had been changed because the original one, also used for the one-day international at the ground in May, had not recovered sufficiently.
Australian captain Mark Taylor asked England to bat first after winning the toss.
